title: Rise of Nationalism and the Moderates

cards.b: Nationalism was not given. It grew from economic grievance, a new English-educated middle class, and a shared fight against colonial rule. The Moderates built the base.

• Economic exploitation shown by the drain theory.
  • Railways, telegraphs and the post made one market.
  • Western ideas, press and the educated class.
  • Racial arrogance, e.g. the Ilbert Bill (1883) controversy.
  • Lytton’s policies: Vernacular Press Act, Arms Act 1878, the cost of the Afghan war.
  • Earlier associations: British Indian Association (1851), Indian Association (1876, Surendranath Banerjea), Poona Sarvajanik Sabha, Madras Mahajan Sabha (1884).

A.O. Hume, a retired civil servant, took the lead. The first session met at Bombay (28 December 1885) under W. C. Bonnerjee, with 72 delegates. Dufferin is said to have approved. Radical writers called it the “safety valve” theory; Bipan Chandra rejects it and says Indian leaders used Hume for their own plans. Early presidents: Naoroji (1886, 1893, 1906), Badruddin Tyabji (1887, first Muslim), George Yule (1888, first English).

Leaders: Dadabhai Naoroji, Pherozeshah Mehta, W. C. Bonnerjee, Surendranath Banerjea, G. K. Gokhale, M. G. Ranade, Romesh Dutt, Madan Mohan Malaviya. Their faith: constitutional agitation, loyalty to the Crown, and the British sense of justice. Methods: prayer, petition, protest. Their demands: expansion of the legislative councils, Indianisation of the ICS and simultaneous exams, cut military costs, protect civil liberties.

• Built a national platform and political education.
  • Economic critique: Naoroji, Dutt, Ranade, G. V. Joshi.
  • Indian Councils Act 1892: more members, right to discuss budget, limited indirect election.
  • Pressure on the Welby Commission (1895).
  • The 1893 Congress under Naoroji; 1905 under Gokhale (Servants of India Society founded the same year).

The Moderates drew support from the educated urban elite only. They had no mass base, believed in the “providential” nature of British rule and won little. The Extremists called their politics “political mendicancy”. Yet Bipan Chandra argues the Moderates did the necessary work: they had to build awareness and a common economic critique first. Lala Lajpat Rai and Tilak later wanted more.

cards.h: Safety valve or seed of freedom?
cards.b: The safety valve idea (Lala Lajpat Rai, 1916; later Marxists) says the Congress was started to channel discontent. Anil Seal (Cambridge School) views early nationalism as elite competition for jobs and offices. Bipan Chandra and others see a genuine anti-colonial movement which used moderate means for strategic reasons.

India’s parliamentary culture, respect for debate and the legal-constitutional style trace to the Moderates. The Servants of India Society idea of public service has echoes in civil society. The Congress, the oldest party, celebrates 28 December as its foundation day.

• “Evaluate the role of the Moderates in the freedom struggle.” Give methods, demands, achievements, limits.
  • “Causes of the rise of Indian nationalism.”
  • Prelims tip: first Congress president (Bonnerjee), first Muslim (Tyabji, 1887), first woman (Annie Besant 1917; Sarojini Naidu first Indian woman, 1925).
